issues.description: signing_mode_enum decision table is incomplete and falls through to CHIP_0002 by coincidence.
issues.detail: Three of four (is_hex, safe_mode) combinations are explicit; the fourth is an unconditional fallthrough return. Readers must enumerate the truth table to confirm correctness. Spell out all four branches (or use an explicit match) so the mapping is a single readable table.

issues.description: sign_message and verify_signature duplicate the same SigningMode-to-bytes dispatch.
issues.detail: Both functions switch on SigningMode to produce the bytes-to-sign, with subtly different branch sets and defaults. Extract a single pure message_bytes(mode, message) -> bytes used by both, so the next CHIP mode is added in one place and the two sides cannot silently disagree.

issues.description: verify_signature docstring still references a 'request' parameter that no longer exists.
issues.detail: The function now takes keyword args (signing_mode, public_key, message, signature, address) but the docstring still reads ':param request:' carried over from the RPC method. Rewrite the docstring to match the new signature or remove it; stale docs are worse than none.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum logic is repeated as a free function and two near-identical property wrappers.
issues.detail: A module-level signing_mode_enum(request) is wrapped by identically named properties on SignMessageByAddress and SignMessageByID that just delegate. Pick one home — direct shared helper or mixin — so maintainers do not have to grep twice to confirm the two paths agree.

issues.description: convert_secret_key_to_synthetic is a Wallet instance method that uses no instance state.
issues.detail: It only calls calculate_synthetic_secret_key with a module-level constant and never touches self. Binding it to Wallet just so the RPC layer can reach it complects identity with a pure value transform. Move it to a module-level function in signing.py (or make it a staticmethod).

issues.description: test_sign_message_by_address never asserts the verify_signature result.
issues.detail: The test awaits verify_signature and discards the returned object. The postcondition under test is isValid=True, but the test passes for any return value including VerifySignatureResponse(isValid=False). Add an explicit assertion on the response so the test actually proves what it claims.

synthesis.summary: The extraction of sign_message and verify_signature into chia/wallet/util/signing.py is the right structural move, but stops one step short of the cleanup that motivates it. The SigningMode-to-bytes dispatch is still duplicated between sign and verify, the new signing_mode_enum helper relies on an implicit fall-through over a four-case truth table, and the helper itself is reachable through three near-identical entry points. Stale docstrings, an instance method with no instance state, and a test that forgets to assert its postcondition round out the polish gaps. Needs-work but small and fixable — land after the duplication and fall-through are tightened.
